steps.detail: ENOENT scandir 'C:\C:\Users\...\cvaa\vaccines' before any antibody ran. Root cause: tools/selftest.mjs line 6 builds its base directory with `new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname` instead of node:url's fileURLToPath(). On Windows this yields a POSIX-style path with a leading slash before the drive letter ('/C:/Users/...'); path.join() on win32 treats that as drive-relative and Node resolves it against the current drive, producing a literal doubled 'C:\C:\...' path that does not exist. Confirmed against the committed bytes (git show HEAD:tools/selftest.mjs) - not a working-copy artifact, not CRLF-related, and not the previously-fixed --experimental-permission/CRLF-frontmatter faults from commit 9065d72 (2026-08-31). tools/replay.mjs (line 10) has the same `.pathname` construction and is independently already known broken per studies/../VERIFICATION.md. tools/fleet.mjs and inoculate.mjs both correctly use fileURLToPath() and were unaffected.
steps.classification: CONFIRMED (real defect, tool crashes on Windows, verified against git HEAD bytes)

caveat_applied: Windows working-copy CRLF is confirmed to produce false findings when an antibody reads file bytes off disk instead of the git blob (README already documents this class: vaccines/202608312252-disk-is-not-what-ships.md). Every finding fleet.mjs produced was re-checked against `git show HEAD:<path>` bytes (or, for git-log-metadata checks, against `git log` output directly, which is immune to working-copy line endings) and classified CONFIRMED / FALSE-CRLF / FALSE (non-CRLF detector bug) / UNVERIFIED. See 202609042153-RUN.md in the coordinator's notes directory for the full per-vaccine table and reasoning; this file records only counts and the two step outcomes.
